subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What should count as sufficient output for this VPS reasoning-latency analysis: a public troubleshooting/runbook doc, new instrumentation spans, or a measured maintainer-run benchmark report?
rationale: The issue asks for analysis and instrumentation across many subsystems, and current source review shows partial existing telemetry but no agreed measurement environment or acceptance threshold.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a bounded Linux/VPS diagnostics runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and identifies measured gaps for later PRs.

options.title: Prioritize instrumentation gaps
options.body: Pick the missing spans maintainers want first and leave measured VPS tuning as a later operator guide.

options.title: Close as support-only
options.body: Treat the concrete CPX32 setup as support tuning outside the repo and ask for fresh trace data before source work continues.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a bounded Linux/VPS diagnostics runbook that maps existing signals to each requested layer and identifies measured gaps for later PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history for the affected diagnostics, context, VPS, and embedded-runner surfaces routes to steipete.
